analysis_type: post-hoc efficiency measurement; fresh sample n cases (paid) + offline token accounting over the sealed run; sealed cache untouched

cache_miss_root_cause.note: Every cache miss traces to the SAME verified root cause, not measurement noise: AgentTools.explain_reasoning() (medguard_v2/agent/clinician_agent.py) gained a new 'step 9' (case_based_explanation: faithful_by_construction + saliency_caveat text) in commit 7f94d9b9 ("feat(v2): N4 trajectory-trust eval (Gap D) + XAI phase-2 case-based explanation", 2026-08-14 23:45:13 +0600) -- confirmed as the sole commit that ever added the string 'case_based_explanation' to this file via `git log --all -S case_based_explanation -- medguard_v2/agent/clinician_agent.py`. This is AFTER the sealed v5.4 cache was written (agent_eval_report_v5_4.json mtime 2026-08-14 19:51, committed as 3aeacead at 20:03:12) by about 3h42m. PROMPT_VERSION was NOT bumped across this change -- it has read "clinician-agent-v5.4" continuously since commit cac3f740 (2026-08-14 18:38:12), before the sealed run and still true at HEAD -- so the cache key's prompt_version pin, which exists precisely to force a regenerate on a version bump, could not and did not catch this: it is a silent behavioural change to a tool's output under an UNCHANGED version label. Any conversation that calls explain_reasoning() sends a DIFFERENT (longer) observation back to the model under current code than the sealed run sent, so every chat() call after that point hashes differently and misses the sealed cache. This is a code-drift artefact of replaying an old cache with current code, not a flaw in this script's cache-key logic -- confirmed by checking every single miss's preceding tool call against agent_eval_report_v5_4.json's own recorded tool_calls.

part2_offline_accounting.tokenizer_used: tiktoken cl100k_base (approximation -- Qwen/Qwen3-32B is not in the local HF cache and this environment does not fetch it over the network)

adjusted_for_truncation.note: raw total + missing_calls_total x mean tokens/call of the calls that DID reconstruct. An extrapolation on top of an approximation -- reported alongside the raw total, not in place of it.

sealed_replay_fidelity_check.note: Diff between this reconstruction's report (endpoints/verification/n_cases/n_questions/question_kinds, everything except the 'rows' text) and the sealed agent_eval_report_v5_4.json. Non-zero diffs here are the DOWNSTREAM effect of the cache_miss_root_cause explain_reasoning drift (54/591 questions truncated early), not an independent discrepancy -- e.g. citation/retrieval/verification counts drop because a truncated question's answer never reaches the point where it would search guidelines or produce a scoreable answer. For the 537/591 (90.9%) UNTRUNCATED questions the replay is exact: same contracts, same cached replies, same scoring, so their tokenized prompts/completions are the REAL sealed conversation.

per_question_avg.note: unique-call real token sum / n_questions -- an amortized average over the sample, not a per-question breakdown (see per_question for that).

latency.wall_clock_note: wall-clock latency is only ever recorded for a call actually made live in SOME process (never persisted into the scratch cache payload); on a run where every unique key's surviving record is a replay (e.g. a pure re-run once the scratch cache is fully populated), per_call_wall_clock_s is legitimately empty/null -- per_call_api_latency_s (persisted in the scratch cache's stored metadata) remains the real, gateway-measured figure regardless of live vs. replay.

cost_estimate_basis.note: real (usage_available) tokens where the gateway returned them, tokenizer estimate otherwise; over the UNIQUE calls (fresh_calls_unique) -- a key reused by more than one question in this sample is billed once, matching what the gateway actually charged.

assumed_rates.source: memory: api-real-pricing (measured gateway pricing, ~40x cheaper than the old $0.01/call heuristic); same rates as efficiency_analysis.json / scripts/dev/finalize_paper_metrics.py.

extrapolation_to_full_sealed_run.method: Linear scaling of this sample's UNIQUE-call cost_estimate_usd by (591 / 58) questions, and separately by (203 / 20) cases. The sample's question-kind mix closely matches the full sealed run's mix (see question_kinds vs. the sealed run's), so linear scaling is a reasonable naive estimate, not a substitute for Part 2's direct reconstruction.
extrapolation_to_full_sealed_run.comparison_to_part2: Part 2 (direct offline reconstruction of the full sealed run) gives $0.3354 raw / $0.3624 truncation-adjusted -- this naive linear extrapolation from Part 1's real measurements is an independent cross-check, not a replacement for Part 2's direct measurement.

calibration.tokenizer_used: tiktoken cl100k_base (approximation -- Qwen/Qwen3-32B is not in the local HF cache and this environment does not fetch it over the network)
calibration.note: ratio = real API-billed tokens / tokenizer-estimated tokens, over the SAME calls, computed with the SAME tokenizer as Part 2. Apply to Part 2's offline totals for a calibrated estimate.

drift_check.note: small-n (fresh sample) comparison against the full 591-question sealed run -- a drift signal, not a statistical claim.

counterfactual_accuracy.note: Ground truth is the host's deterministic aggregator; no judge involved.

absence_disclosure.note: Cases where the corpus holds nothing. Correct behaviour is to say so.

management_fabrication.note: Keyword rule: advice-shaped language in an answer that cites nothing.
